chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
We found in the Book of Ali عليه السلام:
Surely the earth belongs to Allah; He causes whomever He wills from His servants to inherit it, and the end is for the God-conscious.
I and the People of my Household are those whom Allah caused to inherit the earth, and we are the God-conscious, and the whole earth belongs to us.
So whoever among the Muslims revives a land, let him cultivate it, and let him pay its land-tax to the Imam from the People of my Household, and he may keep what he consumes from it.

Then if he abandons it or ruins it, and another man from the Muslims takes it after him and cultivates it and revives it, then he has more right to it than the one who abandoned it. He is to pay its land-tax to the Imam from the People of my Household, and he may keep what he consumes from it, until al-Qa'im from the People of my Household appears with the sword.

Then he will take possession of it, withhold it, and expel them from it, just as the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله did take possession of it and withhold it, except for what is in the hands of our Shi'a; for he will make an arrangement with them regarding what is in their hands, and he will leave the land in their hands.

key_terms.أَحْيَا: revived or restored land to productive use
key_terms.أَهْلُ بَيْتِي: the People of my Household, referring to the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.الْأَرْضَ: the land or earth, understood here as divinely owned and entrusted
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the divinely designated Imam from the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: the Qa'im عليه السلام, who will arise and restore rightful authority
key_terms.الْمُتَّقِينَ: those characterized by taqwa, who are promised the good end
key_terms.خَرَاجَهَا: its land-tax due to the Imam
key_terms.شِيعَتِنَا: our Shi'a, the followers devoted to the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام say about ownership of the earth, reviving land, and the authority of the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Quranic declaration that the earth belongs to Allah through the lens of the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, identifying them as those made to inherit it. It also outlines rulings regarding the revival and cultivation of land, payment of kharaj to the Imam, and the ultimate restoration of full authority over land at the ظهور of al-Qa'im عليه السلام.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Abu Khalid Al Kabuly, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
We<sup>asws</sup> found in the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup> that
[7:128] surely the earth is Allah's; He Causes such of His servants to inherit it as He so Desires, and the end is for those who are pious.

I<sup>asws</sup> and the People<sup>asws</sup> of my<sup>asws</sup> Household are those whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Caused to inherit the earth, and we<sup>asws</sup> are the pious, and the earth, all of it is for us<sup>asws</sup>.

So the one from the Muslims who revives it, so let him build it and let him pay its tax to the Imam<sup>asws</sup> from the People<sup>asws</sup> of my<sup>asws</sup> Household, and for him would be what he consumes from it.

So if he were to neglect it or ruin it, and (another) man from the Muslims was to take it from after him, and he builds it, so he would be more rightful with it than the one who neglected it. He should pay its tax to the Imam<sup>asws</sup> from the People<sup>asws</sup> of my<sup>asws</sup> Household, and for him would be whatever he consumes from it, until there appears Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup> from the People<sup>asws</sup> of my<sup>asws</sup> Household with the sword.

So he<sup>asws</sup> would contain it and prevent it and throw them out from it just as Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> had contained it and prevented it, except what was in the hands of our<sup>asws</sup> Shias, so it would be their piece upon what is in their hands, and he<sup>asws</sup> would leave the land to be in their hands’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from abu Khalid al-Kabuli from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.
“We found in the book of Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.) this.
“The earth belongs to Allah and He gives it in inheritance to whoever of His servants that He wishes. The good end is for those who are pious before Allah’,
I and my Ahl al-Bayt are the people to whom Allah has given the earth in inheritance and we are the ones who are pious before Allah. The whole earth belongs to us.
Thus, whoever of the Muslims would revive a land, he must establish it, pay taxes to the Imam from my Ahl al-Bayt. Whatever he has used would be his.

If he would abandon or allow to become barren and another Muslim would revive and re establish it he will have more right to it than the one who have abandoned. This person will now pay the taxes to the Imam from my Ahl al-Bayt and whatever he would use thereafter is his until Al-Qa’im from my Ahl al-Bayt will rise with Divine Authority and with the sword.

He will control and protect them and will remove from them just as the Messenger of Allah had controlled and protected it, except, however, for what would be in the hands of our followers. He will form a contract with them and will leave the land to them.”
